PTB-Seq is an actual grouped target from the card title, associated with Xue's PTB-directed CLIP-seq rather than treated as an alias for every HITS-CLIP protocol. The primary paper supports UV use and anti-PTB selection, and its Figure S3 caption establishes PTB-bound RNA to cDNA correspondence. The figure supplies 254 nm at the shared schematic level; the inspected PTB main text says UV without specifying wavelength. No supplied PTB passage identifies T1 trimming or explicitly specifies proteinase K. Therefore op_t1 and its downstream local instances op_pk/op_extract/op_rt, whose inputs retain the T1 history, remain family-level depiction and are not assigned to this PTB implementation. PTB RNA-to-cDNA purpose correspondence is supported, but it cannot establish this exact downstream route. The paper's monomer/dimer library separation is unshown and is not added as a diagram branch.

Does the PTB-Seq implementation associated with Xue use RNase T1 trimming and proteinase K, so that the T1-prepared inputs of op_pk, op_extract and op_rt can be assigned to it? The supplied PTB text confirms UV/IP and PTB-bound RNA-derived cDNA but refers the CLIP procedure to Yeo et al. without specifying those transformations. A PTB-specific detailed protocol or its explicitly adopted CLIP protocol identifying the trimming enzyme and protein removal/recovery route is needed. Until then, the exact downstream applicability remains unresolved rather than importing another family member's chemistry.
